interview.hardest_part: Consuming 200 automation science packs requires a complete chain: ore miners feeding furnaces for iron and copper plates, assemblers producing gear wheels and copper wire, more assemblers combining those into science packs, and labs consuming them — all constructed through one screenshot-based input at a time on a Death World Marathon map where biter attacks never pause.
interview.likely_failure: Either a biter attack kills the character before defenses exist (Death World spawns are dense and aggressive), or the assembler and belt layout cannot be placed precisely enough through screenshot targeting to close the automation loop, stalling progress before the automated_iron and science-pack thresholds.
interview.helpful_mechanics: Hold-J mining reliably accumulates ore with a single sustained input; F pickup collects ground items passively; E opens crafting so early iron-plate and gear-wheel milestones can be hit manually before any automation exists; each milestone tier is scored independently so low-end ore counts register points immediately.
interview.harmful_mechanics: One input per turn makes factory construction orders of magnitude slower than a human player; Death World biters are more numerous, more aggressive, and start attacking sooner than a standard map, creating constant lethal pressure; Marathon mode raises all recipe and research costs so the resource volumes needed for upper milestones are much larger; the simulation advances in real time while I reason, so enemies keep moving and attacking between my inputs; precise placement of belts, inserters and assemblers by clicking screenshot pixels is error-prone and a single misplaced tile breaks throughput.
